clean_apply.method: the generated patch reverse-applies cleanly to the current overlay on the pinned base, proving the overlay bytes are exactly the patch result

corpus_qualification: the retained corpus did not contain GOT-relative R_ARM_TARGET2; this milestone is driven by pinned LLD semantics and two relocation-complete Cortex-M3 fixtures, not a frequency or performance claim
scope_limits: the policy is the explicit LLD --target2=got-rel interpretation and is never inferred from an input image
the policy additionally requires the exact retained file-backed non-executable fixed-static firmware GOT graph qualified by --firmbolt-arm-got=fixed-static
dynamic GOT and PLT construction, runtime relocation, symbol interposition and hosted loader behavior remain unsupported
the generic-EHABI fixture covers a retained language-data record while the code fixture covers a relocation word owned by and moved with executable code
the architectural execution fixtures establish the stated relocation, publication and execution properties, not whole-firmware semantic equivalence
the production matrix demonstrates no regression across the existing firmware corpus, not complete x86-backend parity
the milestone establishes reference-graph, relocation, publication and architectural-execution correctness, not a performance result

source.aaelf32: R_ARM_TARGET2 is platform-defined and may select ABS32, REL32 or a GOT-relative expression
source.lld_policy: pinned LLD maps --target2=got-rel to R_ARM_GOT_PREL, whose expression is G(S)+A-P
source.pinned_bolt_gap: BOLT had no ARM backend, no TARGET2 policy and no firmware fixed-GOT binder; v170 added explicit ABS32/REL32 while v173 adds only the explicitly selected GOT-relative form
source.policy_boundary: FirmBOLT preserves relocation type 41 and the logical target while binding through an exact retained firmware slot; it does not silently rewrite the record to R_ARM_GOT_PREL type 96

target2_got_relative_contract.default_policy: reject atomically unless both --firmbolt-arm-target2=got-rel and --firmbolt-arm-got=fixed-static are present
target2_got_relative_contract.handler: BOLT recognizes, sizes, extracts, range-checks and encodes GOT-relative TARGET2 as a PC-relative fixed-GOT request, retains type 41 and target identity, and binds it to the exact qualified firmware slot
target2_got_relative_contract.policy: explicit LLD got-rel TARGET2 semantics plus one exact retained fixed-static firmware GOT graph
target2_got_relative_contract.transformation: one fixture rebuilds generic EHABI while retaining the opaque type-information dependency; the second moves target2_got_worker from 0x08000114 to 0x08000100 and its owned word from 0x08000120 to 0x0800010c without changing the slot, target, relocation type or execution result
